daily_brief: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney addressed the European Parliament in Strasbourg, warmly welcoming the EU's proposal for Canada to become its first 'associate member' — a move that drew threats of 'very serious tariffs' from US President Donald Trump [BBC, RFI]. The proposal reflects deepening transatlantic rifts as both Canada and the EU seek alternatives amid escalating US trade disputes. In Japan, the Bank of Japan raised interest rates to 1.25%, the highest since 1995, signaling continued monetary tightening even as the yen weakened [Financial Times, Nikkei Asia]. Russia began three days of parliamentary voting, with the Kremlin-aligned United Russia party expected to dominate in elections critics dismiss as neither free nor fair; the vote is being framed as a test of public support for the Ukraine war [BBC, Globe and Mail, Al Jazeera]. The EU announced plans to restrict social media access for children under 15, with Commission President von der Leyen proposing 'mini accounts' and strict age verification requirements [BBC]. In South Africa, a ninth woman's body was found near Johannesburg, intensifying fears of a serial killer and reigniting national anger over gender-based violence [BBC, Guardian, RNZ].

top_stories.headline: Canada Welcomes EU 'Associate Member' Proposal as Trump Threatens Tariffs
bullets: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney addressed the European Parliament, welcoming the EU's proposal for Canada to become its first 'associate member' and calling for deeper cooperation on defence, critical minerals, and energy security.
EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed the unprecedented arrangement on Wednesday; no such status currently exists under EU law.
US President Donald Trump called the proposal 'laughable' and threatened 'very serious tariffs' on Europe if he considered it a 'hostile act.'
Canada and the US remain locked in an escalating trade dispute following the collapse of bilateral talks last month.

sources.name: BBC
sources.framing_note: Emphasized warm reception from Carney and geopolitical context of US-Canada trade tensions

sources.name: RFI
sources.framing_note: Highlighted Carney's rejection of US pressure and framed alliance as response to trade 'weaponisation'

top_stories.headline: Bank of Japan Raises Rates to 1.25%, Highest Since 1995
bullets: The Bank of Japan raised its benchmark interest rate to 1.25% in a split vote, marking the highest level since 1995.
Governor Kazuo Ueda stated monetary policy has entered a new phase amid growing upside inflation risks.
The yen weakened following the announcement despite the rate hike.
The move signals the BOJ intends to continue quarterly tightening to keep inflation in check.

sources.name: Financial Times
sources.framing_note: Focused on market reaction and acceleration of tightening cycle

sources.name: Nikkei Asia
sources.framing_note: Emphasized Ueda's comments on policy phase shift and inflation risks

top_stories.headline: Russia Begins Three-Day Parliamentary Vote Amid War and Economic Strain
bullets: Voting began Friday across Russia's 11 time zones for the 450-seat State Duma, the first parliamentary election since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine.
Only parties supporting President Putin and the war in Ukraine are registered to run; the liberal Yabloko party was barred from fielding candidates after a Supreme Court ruling.
The Kremlin is framing the vote as a demonstration of national unity and support for the war effort.
Critics dismiss the election as neither free nor fair; fuel shortages and conscription fears are reported to be unsettling some voters.

sources.name: BBC
sources.framing_note: Described system as 'managed democracy' and noted Kremlin's use of election to claim war support

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Emphasized exclusion of anti-war candidates and economic strain

sources.name: Al Jazeera
sources.framing_note: Focused on pre-election crackdown and suppression of even 'managed opposition'

sources.name: RNZ
sources.framing_note: Straightforward reporting on voting procedures and expected outcomes

sources.name: Financial Times
sources.framing_note: Highlighted fuel queues and conscription fears among voters

top_stories.headline: EU Announces Plan to Restrict Social Media Access for Under-15s
bullets: The European Commission announced plans to ban children under 13 from accessing social media platforms across EU member states.
Children aged 13-15 would be limited to one hour per day via 'mini accounts' set up through a parent's social media account.
Social media companies would be required to prove platforms are safe by design or face fines of up to 6% of global sales.
The legislation, called the EU Kids Act, would affect platforms including TikTok, Instagram, Snapchat, YouTube, AI chatbots, and online games.

sources.name: BBC
sources.framing_note: Presented as child safety measure with quotes from von der Leyen on parental control

top_stories.headline: Ninth Woman's Body Found Near Johannesburg as Serial Killer Fears Grow
bullets: South African police confirmed the discovery of a ninth woman's body in two months in the Ekurhuleni area east of Johannesburg.
Several victims were found partially clothed with signs of injuries; police have not confirmed whether the deaths are connected.
President Cyril Ramaphosa vowed 'no stone will be left unturned' in the investigation.
South Africa has one of the highest femicide rates in the world — 12.2 per 100,000 people in 2022, nearly six times the global rate.

sources.name: BBC
sources.framing_note: Focused on police investigation and presidential response

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Emphasized systemic femicide crisis and women's fear, quoted activists

sources.name: RNZ
sources.framing_note: Straightforward reporting with local resident quotes
